stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
Key technologies involved include transformers and safetensors, central to modern LLM deployment.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: A hacker stole more than 40,000 DHS employee records
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: A major data breach compromised the personal records of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security (DHS) employees.
The stolen data includes sensitive information such as names, job titles, phone numbers, and email addresses.
The breach affects various agencies within DHS, including ICE and CBP.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a ‘significant leap’ in cybersecurity
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Google has launched Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier AI model, emphasizing significant advancements in cybersecurity.
The new model reportedly leads the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0) benchmark, surpassing competitors like Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra.
Key performance improvements highlighted include gains in coding capabilities and agentic task execution.

stories.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
stories.author: arstechnica.com via aCaB
bullet_points: A critical code-execution flaw has been discovered in UEFI firmware.
The vulnerability affects a vast majority of servers globally, indicating widespread risk.
This represents a severe security threat at the foundational hardware level.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the core area of text generation using transformer-based models.
The tags indicate relevance to major open-source AI frameworks like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks requiring context gathering and tool use on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Google says its investments in AI are driving more searches
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google attributes year-over-year growth in search queries to its investments in Artificial Intelligence.
CEO Sundar Pichai highlighted that AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries.
The company reported that its year-over-year query growth rate is the highest among competitors, according to Q3 2026 earnings.

stories.title: Amazon turns its most capable smart speaker into a smart camera, too
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Amazon is integrating camera capabilities into its Echo Studio smart speaker.
The new feature allows the device to 'see and understand' its surroundings.
This represents an expansion of smart home devices into visual AI monitoring.

stories.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
stories.author: Fu-En Yang
bullet_points: ThinkWorld is a new Vision-Language-Action (VLA) learning framework designed to improve robotic manipulation.
It addresses the generalization limitations of current VLA models by leveraging human videos for broader experience.
The core innovation grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strength, mitigating the data vs. grounding trade-off.

stories.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
stories.author: Ying-Cong Chen
bullet_points: Investigates the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) to autonomously discover hidden or altered physical laws.
Introduces 'LongChang,' an automated framework designed to simulate environments with modified physics for testing.
Addresses a fundamental question in AI research: whether LLMs can perform genuine scientific discovery through free exploration.

stories.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
stories.author: Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye
bullet_points: Introduces 'Heads of Security' (HoS), a novel prompt injection defense mechanism for LLMs.
HoS uses learned per-head attention gates to enforce instruction-data separation, allowing models to process untrusted content safely.
The defense is evaluated on large models like Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, showing potential against state-of-the-art attacks.

stories.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
stories.author: Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye
bullet_points: Introduces 'Heads of Security' (HoS), a novel defense mechanism against prompt injection attacks.
HoS uses learned per-head attention gates to enforce instruction-data separation within LLMs.
Evaluated on large models like Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, showing potential superiority over existing defenses.

stories.title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
stories.author: Pratyush Maini
bullet_points: Fine-tuning LLMs on seemingly benign instruction data can silently degrade model safety.
Standard content filters fail to detect this safety degradation because the data appears harmless.
The research introduces SimpleLoRIF, a gradient embedding method to trace safety degradation back to specific fine-tuning examples.

stories.title: Qwenputer: A functioning, deterministic RISC-V CPU inside Qwen3.5
stories.author: csmantle
bullet_points: Integration of a functional, deterministic RISC-V CPU directly within the Qwen3.5 model.
This represents a significant step toward hardware-software co-design in advanced AI systems.
The use of RISC-V suggests an emphasis on open-source, customizable, and efficient compute architecture.

stories.title: Speech models in Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has expanded its capabilities to include support for speech models.
The initial supported model is Phonon from Gradium, enabling text-to-speech functionality.
The implementation offers high performance, streaming audio over 100x faster than real-time on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This integration expands the local and cloud capabilities of the Ollama platform with advanced multimodal AI.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now accessible via Ollama.
Beam is specifically engineered for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is currently offered for free, but only for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the deployment of AI agents using its cloud models.
The integration allows these agents to run securely within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for safe and accessible deployment of AI agents.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weights model ecosystems.

stories.title: Anduril now says its BlueChip laptop will meet Buy American standards at launch
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Anduril and Qualcomm are partnering to develop a BlueChip laptop entirely within the United States.
The initial launch of the fully domestic laptop is slated for 2027.
The partnership signals a broader industry push toward establishing fully domestic supply chains for computing hardware.

stories.title: Akai is embracing vibe-coded mods with an open-source MPC
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Akai is releasing an MPC device with open-source firmware.
The company is actively embracing the custom modding and hacking community.
Early access is being provided to developers to showcase 'vibe-coded' modifications.

stories.title: Readwise is taking on Kindle and Kobo for ebook supremacy
stories.author: David Pierce
bullet_points: Readwise is expanding its ecosystem to directly challenge established e-reader platforms like Kindle and Kobo.
The new offering, Readwise Books, aims to provide a comprehensive reading and knowledge management solution for ebooks.
The company leverages its existing strength in knowledge capture, integrating highlights from Kindle into its broader reading tools.

stories.title: Microsoft reveals strong cloud growth amid financial reporting overhaul
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft reported strong Q1 2027 financial results, achieving $92.3 billion in revenue.
The company saw significant growth, with revenue up 19% and net income increasing by 32%.
Microsoft is undergoing a financial reporting overhaul as part of its new fiscal year structure.

stories.title: Foreign gadget bans: all the news about the FCC’s clampdown on Chinese tech
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The US government is implementing restrictions, effectively creating import bans on certain Chinese consumer electronics.
The crackdown targets various gadgets, including drones, routers, and Roombas.
The issue is framed as a response to US government concerns, potentially signaling broader shifts in tech trade policy.

stories.title: As US ties fray, Europe plans first undersea cable link to Greenland
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Europe is developing the Pan-Arctic Cable, a new undersea infrastructure project.
The cable is strategically designed to bypass US connectivity.
It aims to link major nodes including Canada, Japan, and South Korea.

stories.title: The last, best hope for space tourism just rolled onto a runway in Arizona
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: A new vehicle/technology has arrived in Arizona, potentially marking a significant development for space tourism.
The article addresses the recent lull in commercial space tourism flights.
The development is framed as a 'last, best hope' for advancing the space tourism industry.

stories.title: Google AI gets cagey when asked who won the 2020 elections
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Google's AI exhibits bias in its responses regarding the 2020 US election.
The AI's responses become more direct or neutral when inquiries are directed outside the United States.
The story highlights ongoing concerns about AI model alignment and geopolitical bias.

stories.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
stories.author: Alan Yuille
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hexels,' a novel planar hexagonal surface element designed for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation.
Addresses the high memory and computational demands of modern view synthesis and 3D reconstruction techniques (like radiance fields and splatting).
Hexels achieve efficiency by exploiting locally planar regions using fewer, larger primitives with a first-order spatial color field.

stories.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
stories.author: Zhi-Song Liu
bullet_points: KPPax bridges the gap between traditional atmospheric chemistry modeling (KPP language) and modern differentiable programming frameworks used in ML.
It translates KPP-defined kinetic mechanisms into differentiable, JAX-compiled, and vectorizable code.
The tool enables the integration of complex chemical rate laws directly into machine learning workflows for atmospheric science.

stories.title: What Improves During Pretraining? Tracking Knowledge Acquisition with Point-in-Time Models
stories.author: Yao Lu
bullet_points: The research investigates how different types of knowledge (general vs. domain-specific) are acquired during large language model pretraining.
The study utilizes 'point-in-time models' trained on web snapshots from various years to track knowledge evolution over time.
A new metric, the Temporal Variability Score (TVS), is proposed to quantify how the prevalence of specific knowledge items changes across training periods.

stories.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
stories.author: Khalil El Khammar
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical issue in LLM group decision-making: how to effectively compress complex discussions into a short memory for a final decision-maker.
It investigates two heuristics for memory compression—retaining the rarest claims or claims relevant to decision criteria—and notes their ambiguity in hidden-profile tasks.
The authors introduce 'CrossProfile,' a new diagnostic benchmark with 60 templates to rigorously test these memory and decision-making failures in LLMs.

stories.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
stories.author: Shilei Wen
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) where language-based reasoning causes 'visual forgetting' in video understanding.
Existing methods for maintaining visual grounding are limited, often relying on symbolic textual coordinates to reference visual evidence.
VideoLVR proposes a new approach to enable models to reliably revisit relevant visual evidence during complex video reasoning tasks.

stories.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
stories.author: Alan Yuille
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hexels,' a novel planar hexagonal surface element designed for efficient 3D scene representation.
Addresses the high memory and computational demands of modern view synthesis techniques like radiance fields and splatting.
Hexels leverage locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance to reduce the number of necessary primitives.

stories.title: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
stories.author: Yu Chen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the instability of test-time adaptation (TTA), where interventions can help one batch but harm the next.
Traditional metrics like average accuracy fail to capture these localized failures, necessitating a smarter intervention strategy.
The authors propose PORTAL, a controller designed to intelligently decide when and how to apply model interventions, moving beyond reliance on scarce target labels.

stories.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
stories.author: Claire Tomlin
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of current robotic manipulation, specifically in complex, dexterous in-hand object maneuvering.
The study focuses on 'in-hand object pose reaching,' a challenging task requiring diverse and precise grasps.
A key contribution is addressing the critical, yet often unmeasured, aspect of safety during these complex robotic tasks.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
stories.author: Alexander Toshev
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of building high-performing LLM agents capable of complex, multi-step tasks using tools.
It introduces SynthAPI, a pipeline designed to control the diversity of synthetically generated tool-use training environments.
The study investigates how varying environment composition (tools, tasks, databases) impacts agent training performance.

stories.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
stories.author: Mingyi Hong
bullet_points: The research introduces MuonGS, a method for pretraining Large Language Models (LLMs) using relaxed weight-norm control.
It addresses the incomplete understanding of why weight decay and explicit weight-norm constraints improve optimizer performance in LLM training.
The study analyzes norm control across the training trajectory using a novel metric: the accumulated effective learning rate ($C_T$).

stories.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
stories.author: Rui Wu
bullet_points: Introduces GAS-PFN, a novel network for zero-shot traffic forecasting that addresses the limitations of traditional supervised graph models.
The model leverages Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) to enable deployment to new or evolving road networks without extensive retraining.
It specifically models complex spatiotemporal dynamics by incorporating graph-aware mechanisms to capture road topology dependencies.

stories.title: Understanding the limits of latent world models
stories.author: Steffen Schneider
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in current world model research: most evaluations focus on task performance rather than the quality of the learned latent dynamics.
It introduces the concept of 'faithful latent world models' to better assess model quality.
Faithfulness is defined using an equivariance condition between the true environment transition map and the model's learned latent dynamics.

stories.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
stories.author: Amir Gholami
bullet_points: Addresses limitations in current LLM agent learning by recognizing that not all failures provide useful signals.
Proposes 'GEPA-Curator' to curate tasks for self-improving agents, moving beyond simple learning from failed rollouts.
Highlights that agent failures can stem from prompt weaknesses, harness limitations, or noisy execution, not just the agent's logic.

stories.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
stories.author: Ying-Cong Chen
bullet_points: The research explores whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can autonomously discover hidden or altered physical laws.
A framework named LongChang is introduced to simulate environments with modified physics for testing.
The core hypothesis tests the LLM's ability to detect anomalous behavior and formulate new scientific questions without prior guidance.

stories.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
stories.author: Zhiwei Deng
bullet_points: Addresses the quadratic time complexity bottleneck of self-attention in long-sequence modeling for LLMs.
Introduces 'Multi-State Linear Attention' (MSLA) to improve efficiency by segmenting and compressing context.
The proposed method aggregates segment information using mean alignment between queries and segment keys.

stories.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
stories.author: Dimitris N. Metaxas
bullet_points: Introduces a 'metacognitive controller' to guide diffusion language model generation.
The controller optimizes computational efficiency by determining when to finalize tokens and generation length.
Aims to improve the efficiency of diffusion language agents during interaction with an environment.

stories.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
stories.author: Khalil El Khammar
bullet_points: The paper investigates how memory compression affects the decision-making process of LLM groups.
It proposes two heuristics (keeping rarest claims or claims relevant to criteria) that are attractive but potentially flawed.
A new diagnostic benchmark, CrossProfile, is introduced to test these memory and decision-making failures.

stories.title: Teach reality, not ethics: a drop-in continued-pretraining corpus installs coupled human-biosphere-AI welfare dispositions across model families
stories.author: Mingxun Wang
bullet_points: Addresses the gap in current LLM training regarding ecological reasoning and impact on living systems.
Introduces a novel 'coupled welfare' corpus designed for continued pre-training, integrating human, biosphere, and AI dependency data.
Aims to mitigate the risk of LLMs making irreversible decisions that harm living systems under operational pressure.

stories.title: The Grid, a factory-scale robot in Massachusetts that builds PCBs on demand
stories.author: seddona
bullet_points: Introduction of 'The Grid,' a factory-scale robotic system.
The system is designed to build Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) on demand.
The technology is based in Massachusetts, indicating industrial automation advancements.

stories.title: Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
stories.author: emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com by galadran
bullet_points: The news concerns a security vulnerability within Apple's Git implementation.
The vulnerability involves Apple's Git trusting compromised eMudhra certificates.
This highlights a potential weakness in how Apple handles certificate trust in development tools.

stories.title: How to cut your AI agent's input tokens: what worked, what failed, and a bench to measure yours
stories.author: anis_meziani_52aab42304a8
bullet_points: Addresses the critical operational cost issue of large AI agent token consumption.
Provides practical, real-world insights from a production field report on token reduction techniques.
Offers a measurable framework (a 7-point checklist and open-source bench) for readers to benchmark their own agents.

stories.title: Built for Humans, Flooded by Agents: Why Git Infrastructure Is Being Rebuilt
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: Anthropic is undergoing a significant infrastructure overhaul for its monorepo.
The article discusses the challenges of managing high volumes of code changes (2,500/day) in large repositories.
The theme suggests a shift or necessity to rebuild Git infrastructure to support advanced AI development.
